mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES recorded a monotone three-week recovery from -41.1 to -30.6 percent, which restores weekday commuting routines; returning commuters generate weekday footfall in retail corridors, so the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC must exceed the last 28-day mean of roughly -36.7.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose +10.5 points from t-3w (-41.1) to t-0w (-30.6) with no weekly reversal
failure_condition: The next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is less than or equal to -36.7, i.e. no gain despite WORKPLACES continuing to sit at or above its t-0w level of -30.6.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT has cleared the -73.0 threshold in two consecutive weeks (-72.3 then -71.4) after months below it; crossing this level marks transit use shifting from essential-only to discretionary trips, which is what actually feeds retail-and-recreation venues, so RETAIL_REC rises over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean stays above -73.0 for two consecutive weeks (currently -72.3 then -71.4)
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose monotonically -75.0, -74.1, -72.3, -71.4 and cleared -73.0 in the last two weeks
failure_condition: Within two weeks of TRANSIT holding above -73.0, the trailing 14-day mean of RETAIL_REC fails to rise above its value at the crossing week.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL has fallen monotonically from +19.6 to +16.4, a three-week decline of 3.2 points, which measures households substituting time out of the home for time at home; the substitution directs discretionary hours toward retail and recreation venues and lifts RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL continues to fall to +15.0 or below while the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC stays below -36.7, showing out-of-home substitution is not flowing to retail.

mechanism_narrative: Retail-and-recreation recovery requires commuting and non-commuting transit demand to improve jointly; only when WORKPLACES and TRANSIT rise in the same week does the combined commuter-plus-shopper flow materialize, and both have risen together in each of the last three weeks, so RETAIL_REC moves higher over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both post a week-on-week improvement in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improved in each of the t-2w, t-1w and t-0w intervals
regime_hint: reopening with simultaneous workplace and transit gains
failure_condition: The next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is not higher than -36.7 even though WORKPLACES and TRANSIT continue to improve jointly for at least two more weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Restrictions are being relaxed on a schedule that first releases workplaces and only then discretionary venues; conditional on RESIDENTIAL dropping below +17.0, which signals the release of stay-at-home mandates, the lagged easing of retail capacity binds within two weeks and RETAIL_REC rises.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean falls below +17.0 (currently +16.4) while WORKPLACES stays at or above -32.0
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL crossed below +17.0 at t-0w while WORKPLACES stood at -30.6
regime_hint: active policy relaxation sequencing workplaces before discretionary capacity
failure_condition: In the two weeks after RESIDENTIAL is below +17.0 with WORKPLACES at or above -32.0, the 14-day mean of RETAIL_REC does not improve relative to the crossing week.

mechanism_narrative: Autumn cooling pushes outdoor activity indoors; PARKS has already rolled over from -13.6 to -17.0, and each further multi-point drop in park visits substitutes discretionary leisure hours into indoor retail-and-recreation venues, raising RETAIL_REC over the following four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean falls by 3 or more points versus the prior week (observed: -13.6 to -17.0)
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS reversed from -13.6 at t-2w to -17.0 at t-0w
regime_hint: seasonal transition to cooler weather reducing outdoor activity
failure_condition: Following a PARKS drop of 3 or more points week-on-week, the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is lower than the prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM sitting essentially at baseline (-1.9 to -0.3) shows that essential-goods shopping has fully normalized; households that no longer need to consolidate trips into grocery runs reallocate marginal shopping trips to retail venues within one week, lifting RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM weekly mean stays within 2 points of baseline (above -2.0)
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM remained between -1.9 and -0.3 across all four weeks
regime_hint: essential-goods shopping fully normalized to pre-period baseline
failure_condition: While GROCERY_PHARM remains above -2.0, the week-on-week change in RETAIL_REC is zero or negative for the following week.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has decoupled from the mobility recovery: WORKPLACES gained 10.5 points over three weeks while RETAIL_REC moved only 1.7 points, so incremental mobility is commuting-only and adds no discretionary retail demand; the series is saturating near -36, and the next 28-day mean prints at or below the last 28-day mean.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES improves 5 or more points over three weeks while RETAIL_REC changes by less than 2 points over the same span
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES +10.5 points versus RETAIL_REC +1.7 points over the same three-week window
regime_hint: saturated recovery where mobility gains no longer convert into retail footfall
failure_condition: The next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC exceeds -36.0 while WORKPLACES and RETAIL_REC remain decoupled over the next two weeks.
